title: Slot-based response lease and SDK layout (PRD sketch)
body:
Goal
------
Capture a compact, developer-ergonomic model for streaming responses that treats partial output as leased "slots" and gives SDKs a simple, deterministic contract for tool calls, retries, resumability, and structured output validation. This doc is an early PRD sketch to align product + eng on minimal API semantics, observability, and rollout path.

Motivation / problem statement
-----------------------------
Current hosted streaming semantics are powerful but leave client behavior underspecified when:
- the model emits partial structured data and then changes the schema mid-stream,
- a tool call is requested while network connectivity is flaky,
- we need low-latency fallbacks to smaller models without violating client expectations,
- mobile/edge SDKs want a small surface area to reason about incremental update durability.

We need a predictable, low-mental-overhead contract: clients should be able to decide whether to commit partial results, re-request missing slots, or gracefully fall back to a higher-latency reconciliation path.

Key proposal (summary)
----------------------
Introduce a lightweight "response lease" primitive layered on top of the streaming API: the server issues numbered slots (lease IDs) for discrete logical fragments (text blocks, JSON records, action frames). Each slot has a short-lived lease TTL and a durability hint (best-effort | durable). SDKs expose high-level primitives around slots: commit(slot), extend(slot), replace(slot), and abort(slot). Tool calls are attached to slots (tool:slot_id) and inherit the slot's lifecycle.

Why this helps
- Deterministic replay: when a connection breaks we can resume by negotiating the last-committed slot id.
- Tool safety: tools invoked for uncommitted slots can be marked speculative and optionally cancelled on resume.
- Graceful fallbacks: routing policy can route new slots to cheaper model variants while still honoring committed slots from a higher-fidelity model.

Non-goals
---------
- This PRD is not trying to solve long-term distributed transaction semantics across multiple tools.
- Not introducing heavy server-side session storage for every free-form stream (we prefer compact resume tokens).

API surface (sketch)
-------------------
Server -> Client (stream events):
- slot_open: {slot_id, type: text|json|action, lease_ms, durability_hint}  (server opens a slot)
- slot_patch: {slot_id, patch_delta}  (incremental content for slot)
- slot_commit: {slot_id, canonical_schema?}  (server indicates slot committed)
- slot_abort: {slot_id, reason}
- tool_request: {tool_call_id, slot_id, tool_name, args}  (server asks client-side tool to run)

Client SDK primitives (minimal model):
- onSlotOpen(cb(slotMeta))  // receive and render partials
- commitSlot(slot_id) -> ack token  // client indicates it persisted or accepted slot
- extendSlot(slot_id, extra_ms)  // request a lease extension (best-effort)
- resumeSession(resume_token, last_known_committed_slot)  // resume after disconnect
- runToolForSlot(slot_id, tool_name, args, opts) -> tool_call_id  // run a local/integrated tool
- toolResult(tool_call_id, result) -> optional server acknowledgement

Streaming semantics notes
------------------------
- Lease TTLs are intentionally short (e.g., 30s default) to avoid long-lived server memory pressure; SDKs should auto-extend during active UI interactions.
- Durability hint = "best-effort" (render-only) or "durable" (client should commit before trusting the value). The server chooses hint per slot based on model confidence and cost.
- If a slot expires without commit, server may emit slot_abort. Client should keep last known content but present it as potentially stale.

Tool calling and speculative execution
-------------------------------------
- Tool requests are bound to a slot_id. When a tool_request is emitted for a slot with durability_hint=best-effort, client SDK should default to speculative local execution unless configured otherwise.
- If a tool call requires durability (e.g., billing, database write), server will request it on a slot flagged durable; SDK should prompt developer or toggle a flag to block speculative execution.
- Tool call lifecycle: request -> run (local or proxied) -> result -> tool_ack -> tool_commit. If connection drops mid-call, client can retry by referencing tool_call_id within resumeSession. Server will deduplicate by tool_call_id (idempotency).

Structured output and schema evolution
-------------------------------------
- slot_commit can optionally include a schema hash. When the schema hash changes mid-session, SDKs surface a single event: onSchemaDrift(old_hash,new_hash,slot_id). Developer can choose to re-validate UI or request a canonicalization API call.
- We recommend JSON-LD / small schema bundles as the canonical structured output format for committed slots (compact and self-describing).

SDK ergonomics and recommended defaults
--------------------------------------
- High-level SDKs (JS, iOS, Android) should expose the slot primitives but provide opinionated helpers: streamingText(slot) aggregator, optimisticToolRunner(toolName) wrapper, and autoResume/resumeDialog helpers.
- Default UX: render partials immediately, show ephemeral loading indicators for uncommitted slots, and persist committed slots to local storage for quick resume.
- Small footprint mobile client: allow a "lite" mode where SDK only tracks last N committed slot_ids and uses a stateless resume token instead of full per-slot state.

Observability and telemetry
--------------------------
- Emit telemetry events at slot_open, slot_commit, slot_abort, slot_extend, tool_request, tool_result, resume_attempt (with outcome) and schema_drift. These will be surfaced in Console with per-session timelines.
- Tag telemetry with: session_id, slot_id, model_variant, route (hosted/dedicated), latency_ms (time from slot_open to commit), and durability_hint.

Rollout plan (phased)
---------------------
1) Canary API flags for slot events on a small subset of Hosted customers; SDK opt-in flag.
2) Expand to beta customers and add server-side resume token support.
3) Turn on default durability hints for server-generated tool calls and ship high-level SDK helpers.
4) Migrate Console UIs to show slot timelines and per-slot cost/latency.

Open questions / trade-offs
-------------------------
- Lease duration defaults: 15s vs 30s vs 60s (balance latency vs server memory).
- How much state do we persist server-side for resumability? Compact resume tokens vs server ledger for last N slots.
- Idempotency: require globally unique tool_call_id from client or allow server-generated ids? (trade-off: complexity vs safety).
- Schema bundling format: full JSON-LD vs lightweight typed proto.

Immediate next steps / action items
----------------------------------
- Product: consolidate UX patterns for ephemeral vs durable slots (Maya) — due 2025-07-09.
- Eng serving-runtime: prototype slot events over existing streaming protocol, measure server memory and resume token size (Diego) — POC by 2025-07-30.
- SDK leads: mock JS and mobile primitives and developer-facing docs (Priya) — demo 2025-08-06.
- Solutions engineering: identify 3 early beta customers and gather failure-mode requirements (Noah) — outreach by 2025-07-15.

Notes / rough sketches
---------------------
- Example quick flow: model opens slot S1 (text, lease 30s, best-effort). client renders partial, auto-extends while user types. model emits tool_request bound to S1 for "search-db". SDK runs local simulator -> tool_result returned quickly. model later commits S1 with schema hash H1. Client commitSlot(S1) persists local record. On resume after disconnect, client sends last_committed = S1 and resume_token. Server responds only with newer slots.

- If S1 had been durable and tool_call caused an external side-effect, server will require tool_commit acknowledgement before marking commit.

Appendix: UX examples (short)
---------------------------
- Chat UI: each bubble maps to a slot. Uncommitted bubbles show a pulsing dot; committed bubbles show a check icon and are pinned in transcript.
- Form-filling: server streams JSON slots for individual fields; client can persist each committed slot as partial form save.

This is intentionally lightweight — aim is to converge on simple primitives that SDKs can implement robustly. Feedback welcome, especially from SDK/mobile leads and serving-runtime on memory/latency implications.
